name: Idle resource reclaimer — inventory, propose, human approves, verify
_why: The full eight-phase lifecycle, and the only case in this suite that
changes anything. It pins the sequence an operator actually sees:
1  TRIAGE -> GATHER parks holding the INVENTORY (read-only)
2  results -> HYPOTHESIZE -> PLAN -> GATE parks holding the RECLAIM,
and the run is reported in phase ACT because a human now owns it
3  APPROVED comes back -> ACT -> VERIFY parks holding the inventory AGAIN
4  results -> REPORT, with the deletion proved by absence, not by exit code
Two things here would be silent regressions anywhere else. The gated call
carries the automation's REAL argument names — PLAN is shown the schema,
and without that a model invents 'region'/'volumes' and every gated action
fails input validation on arrival. And VERIFY re-runs the read-only
inventory rather than trusting the reclaim's own success line.

tools.name: workflow_51
tools.description: Lists unattached EBS volumes, unassociated elastic IPs and stopped instances in one region, with age, tags and an indicative monthly cost per item. Read-only.

tools.name: workflow_52
tools.description: Deletes named unattached EBS volumes after taking and CONFIRMING a recovery snapshot of each. Report-only unless Execute is true. Acts only on the exact volume ids supplied.

event.input: Reclaim what is safe to reclaim in us-east-1. The staging fleet was decommissioned last quarter.

value.restated: Find unattached EBS volumes in us-east-1 that are genuinely abandoned and reclaim only those.
observations_needed: The current inventory of unattached volumes, with age, tags and size

script.text: Taking the inventory first. Nothing is proposed until I have seen it.

script.text: The inventory is in. I have what I need to decide.

findings.summary: Three volumes are genuinely abandoned: vol-0a1b2c3d4e5f67890, vol-0b2c3d4e5f6789012 and vol-0c3d4e5f67890123a have been unattached for a year or more and two of them carry decommissioned staging names.
vol-0d4e5f6789012345b is tagged to the data-platform team, so it needs their sign-off rather than a deletion, despite being the largest single cost here.
vol-0e5f67890123456cd was detached 9 days ago, which is short enough to be a migration in progress rather than waste.

arguments.Reason: Reclaiming disks from the staging fleet decommissioned last quarter

actions.intent: Delete the three volumes that have been unattached for over a year, after taking a confirmed recovery snapshot of each.
actions.blast_radius: 260 GB across three EBS volumes in us-east-1 is deleted. Nothing is attached to them, so no running workload is interrupted. Any data on them is reachable afterwards only through the recovery snapshots.
actions.rollback: One retained snapshot per volume, taken and confirmed complete before each deletion. A volume can be recreated from its snapshot; recreating it does NOT reattach it to anything or restore whatever was using it. Once the snapshots are also deleted there is no way back.

script.text: Confirmed — none of the three appear in the fresh inventory.

**Three abandoned volumes deleted and confirmed gone; two were deliberately left alone.**

| Volume | Size | Idle | Recovery snapshot |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| vol-0a1b2c3d4e5f67890 | 100 GB | 412 days | snap-0abc1 [e:901] |
| vol-0b2c3d4e5f6789012 | 100 GB | 388 days | snap-0abc2 [e:901] |
| vol-0c3d4e5f67890123a | 60 GB | 355 days | snap-0abc3 [e:901] |

Verified by re-running the inventory: none of the three appear in it any more [e:902].

Left alone on purpose:

- vol-0d4e5f6789012345b is tagged to the data-platform team, so it needs their sign-off rather than a deletion — and at 500 GB it is the largest single item on the list [e:900].
- vol-0e5f67890123456cd was detached 9 days ago, which is short enough to be a migration in progress [e:900].

The inventory total fell from 78.00 to 56.00 [e:900][e:902]. Those are published us-east-1 list prices rather than this customer's negotiated rate, so treat them as the size of the prize and not as a billing figure.

Next step: the three recovery snapshots are retained. Delete them once someone is satisfied nothing on those disks was needed.
